title: I announced my new game, where I used AI to create game covers, a feature that wouldn't be practical at this scale otherwise
author: BootPhaseGames

comments.author: BootPhaseGames
comments.body:
I'm developing a game where you produce videogames and can design their game covers. In addition, there are up to 100 NPC competitors producing games with covers as well.  
  
To execute my vision, I need hundreds of different game cover images, on top of which the player inserts their title dynamically using different predefined art styles.

I think it's interesting because that's the kind of feature that would not be feasible for a solo developer without AI generation. Consider that there are tens of genres and topics, plus different gaming generations have different styles. This requires a lot of curated generation to make sure the art styles make sense.

For as solo developer who's doing this during his free time, it's not feasible to commission the hundreds of art pieces that are required to have a system of non-repeated game covers, when there are also tens of genres and topics and NPC competitors releasing games as well. What I can guarantee is that I am curating the covers I generate, to make sure they match the genre, topic and gaming generation they belong to.

Of course, I am receiving some hateful messages. The irony is, this feature would not exist without AI. So they would never the play in any case.

replies.author: Bapstien
replies.body:
Ok but a lot of other assets are also AI-generated and your AI disclaimer doesn't really talks about it

 maybe that's why some hateful message are there

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
This isn't true though. If a dev wanted to do this before AI it would just take longer and require choosing a cover art direction that was simpler and quicker and easier to produce.

If you say it wouldn't be practical to produce covers of this complexity then that's true but nobody would do that to begin with anyway unless they had an art team. You are inventing a problem and then saying AI was the solution.

All you have actually done is add a lot of obvious AI generated images to your game which people are going to notice and have opinions about. 

For a game like this you would have been much better off going for a more minimalist type of art style. 

Something like these: https://www.europosters.eu/car-minimalist-movie-poster-12261/

That way not only would it fit the game art style better but you could also use some AI to help speed up the process without them ending up looking like typical AI generated images.

replies.author: BootPhaseGames
replies.body: Your suggestion works for abstract things like genres, not game cover images.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: The link I posted is an example of movie posters not genres so it would work for cover images too.

replies.author: BootPhaseGames
replies.body: I'll think about it, thanks for the feedback. Although I'm not convinced that simplifying the art style of the covers fits my vision.

replies.author: loulibra
replies.body: surely no human could imagine 100 images for game covers!  inconcieveable!!
